summary.text: Melissa Ziobron is the Republican and Independent Party of Connecticut candidate for the Connecticut House of Representatives, District 34, in the November 3, 2026 general election, where she faces Democrat Meghan Rosenfeld in a race with no incumbent.
She previously represented District 34 in the Connecticut House from 2013 to 2019.

paragraphs.text: Ziobron graduated from Nathan Hale-Ray High School in 1989 and earned a degree in zoology from Central Connecticut State University.
She was the first economic development coordinator for the town of East Haddam.
Ziobron was first elected to the House in 2012, defeating Democrat Christopher Goff, and took office on January 9, 2013.
She won re-election in 2014 and 2016 and served on the Appropriations, Environment and other committees, including as ranking member of Appropriations in the 2015 and 2017 sessions.
In 2018 she ran for Connecticut State Senate District 33 and lost to Norm Needleman by 85 votes, 50.1 percent to 49.9 percent; she left the House on January 9, 2019.
